title: Joint operating agreement and escalation
objective: Resolve a disagreement about promising a write-back integration.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: When two organizations work one account, ambiguity costs time and credibility. A short operating agreement before delivery prevents most problems.

items: **Customer communications:** who sends what, and who is copied.
**Artifact storage:** where the use case log, workflow maps, and value model live, and who can see them.
**Technical answers:** who answers feasibility and product questions, and how unresolved ones are tracked.
**Value review:** who checks assumptions and evidence labels before anything reaches the customer.
**Approvals:** which decisions need Glean's internal approval, such as pilots, pricing, and roadmap statements.
**Follow-up:** who owns the recap and the mutual action plan after each session.

blocks.x: Keep a decision log. When the team disagrees, or a product or policy question is unresolved, escalate it. Don't guess in front of the customer. One accountable owner per decision is better than shared ambiguity.

blocks.label: Example
blocks.x: A partner believes a custom data source is supported, but the SE hasn't verified it. Log feasibility as unresolved, assign technical validation, and keep the first-wave scope conditional until the answer is documented.
Agree the operating rules before the first customer session, not during an escalation.

blocks.title: Joint operating agreement
blocks.alt: Six cards listing what Glean and the partner agree up front: who sends customer communications, where artifacts are stored, who answers technical questions, who reviews value claims, who approves commitments, and who owns follow-up.
